newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Feb 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Feb 13.

text.p: Mitsubishi Corp has decided to withdraw from the pre-paid pinball card business due to losses from fake cards and mounting public criticism of trading companies for engaging in the pinball business. It may sell its shares in an affiliate, Japan Leisure Card System Co Ltd (Japan LEC), an issuer of the pre-paid cards. As of the end of September 1996, Japan LEC was suffering from 46 billion yen in excess liabilities over assets due to pinball card forgery.

Itochu Corp has set up a joint venture to enter the worldwide shipping container leasing business as early as the end of February. The company, capitalised at 6.4 billion yen, is owned 45 percent by each Itochu and Prudential Asset Management Co Ltd and the rest by other Japanese leasing companies. It will lease steel, refrigerator and open-top containers to shipping companies and container depots.

Takeda Chemical Industries Ltd is expected to increase its consolidated net profit by 17 percent to 70 billion yen in the year to March 1997, 4.5 billion yen more than it initially projected. This is due to robust sales of medical products in the United States and the yen"s weakness.

Nissan Chemical Industries Ltd is expected to enjoy a record 6.8 billion yen pre-tax profit in the year to March 1997, up 19 percent from a year ago, helped by growing demand for electronics materials and improved earnings due to the yen"s weakness.

Tsumura & Co is expected to report a group net loss around 1.5 billion yen in the year to March 1997 as a result of liquidating loss-making subsidiaries. It will be the plans to liquidate Tsumura Illusion, a Tokyo-based arts dealer, by the end of March.
